questions.answer: Glamorgan Archives stated "These points were answered in my email of 14th September." That reply covered the examination and photography of DBDT/79/1 (catalogued May 1877, Pembroke Terrace) and included a digital photography order form.

questions.text: Is DBDT79/1 a lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Marquess of Bute's trustees and Mr John Williams?
questions.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives confirmed: “The document is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport.”

questions.text: What is the exact property description in deed DBDT79/1, and does it locate the property in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff?
questions.answer: Yes, the deed locates the property in Pembroke Terrace. questions.text: Does deed DBDT79/1 mention Llandough, Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Western Ground Rents, or other localities?
questions.answer: No. Glamorgan Archives confirmed: “There is no mention of Llandough, Great House Farm or Ty Mawr or any other property outside of Pembroke Terrace.”

questions.text: Does the marginal plan on DBDT79/1 clearly identify the property's location?
questions.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives said: “The plan clearly shows a property on Pembroke Terrace.” A digital copy could be supplied for a charge of £15.60 (inclusive of VAT).

questions.text: Does DBDT79/1 include further details like adjoining owners, plot numbers, rent or cross-references?
questions.answer: No. Glamorgan Archives stated: “There is no further information included,” beyond the description already quoted from the deed.

questions.text: Was the DBDT79/1 catalogue description, which named only 'the Marquess of Bute' rather than his trustees, correct?
questions.answer: No; Glamorgan Archives confirmed the catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 'had a few small errors which have now been corrected' and that the document is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport.

questions.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not confirm whether such a record exists, stating only: “If any record of this is in our collections it would appear in the Planning Committee records described above in point 6,” without confirming a specific record had been found.

questions.answer: Yes. Glamorgan Archives identified the relevant items as DXJF/64/30-31: “sketch of former layout of part of village of Llandough-juxta-Penarth by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of great house farm, Llandough, with notes c1950 [1 card, 1 paper].” It asked the requester to confirm whether this matched material already seen, noting the other items in the bundle do not relate to Llandough.

questions.text: Does Glamorgan Archives list any deeds, besides DBDT10/19 and DBDT10/20, linking the Thomases to the Bute Estate?

questions.text: Does Glamorgan Archives hold Daniel Thomas's will linking him to the Llandough lime works or Great House Farm?
questions.answer: Glamorgan Archives did not supply or confirm holding such a will. questions.text: Did the Bute Estate later reacquire any parcel of land previously linked to Daniel Thomas?

questions.text: What identifying details does deed DBDT10/19 give for Daniel Thomas?
questions.answer: Glamorgan Archives confirmed that DBDT/10/19 describes Daniel Thomas as “of the Town of Cardiff, Builder” and that “There are no further identifying details for Daniel Thomas in the documents.” Digital copies could be supplied for a charge, or the documents viewed free of charge in the public searchroom.

questions.answer: No extant record exists apart from a brief note. RCAHMW stated: “No record of the C.N. Johns / Mrs Buckler correspondence or allusion to the same is extant in our records, with the exception of the brief note in Archive 6048945.”

questions.text: Does archive 6048945 record the date, purpose, or materials from the December 1988 site visit to Great House Farm?
questions.answer: No. RCAHMW said archive 6048945 is one page, front and back, and there is no surviving record giving the date or purpose of the visit beyond the description currently catalogued, nor any associated site note, field sheet, photograph, sketch or correspondence.

questions.text: Do RCAHMW's internal records for the Great House Farm accession numbers hold anything beyond what Coflein publishes?
questions.answer: No. RCAHMW said its searches of internal records relating to these accession numbers revealed no further information beyond the public catalogue, and confirmed again that it holds nothing beyond the material already visible on Coflein.

questions.text: Do archive records 6364275 and 6364276 relate to Great House Farm, Llandough?
questions.answer: No. RCAHMW said these records had been thoroughly and physically reviewed and relate to the sites stated in the catalogue, which it identified as Tŷ Mawr, Tresimwn, and 33 Whitecross Street, Monmouth; they do not relate or allude to Great House Farm, Llandough, in any way.

questions.text: Does RCAHMW hold aerial photographs that show Great House Farm, Llandough, in detail?
questions.answer: RCAHMW said any aerial photographs covering the site would likely be high-altitude verticals unlikely to show the site in detail, and that it holds no further photographic record of the site in its collection.

questions.text: What are the archive reference numbers for the 1974 investigator's notes and the 1988 ink plan of Great House Farm?
questions.answer: RCAHMW said the 1974 investigator's notes by H.J. Thomas are archive 6048943, and the ink plan with additions made on 12/12/1988 is archive 6048941; it holds nothing beyond the material already visible on Coflein for these items.

questions.text: Does RCAHMW hold any record of transfers, retention or disposal decisions for the Great House Farm archive material?

questions.text: Does RCAHMW hold provenance information for the nineteenth-century armour deposit account from Great House Farm?

questions.text: Has RCAHMW confirmed its searches for Great House Farm records are complete and that nothing is being withheld?

questions.text: What search terms, repositories and functions did the NPCC consult in responding to FOI 3065/2026?
questions.answer: The NPCC disclosed its search methodology, listing two search terms, five repositories/source descriptions, and four consulted functions used to respond to the request.

questions.text: Does the NPCC hold information responsive to questions 4 to 6 of FOI 3065/2026?
questions.answer: No. The NPCC said that information relating to Q4–Q6 'is not held'. It also supplied, as a goodwill gesture, the policing-lead retrieval email, and noted that search results had already been captured by email in earlier disclosures.

questions.text: Did the NPCC uphold its substantive response to FOI 3156/2026 on internal review?
questions.answer: Yes. The NPCC's internal review upheld the substantive response given under FOI 3156/2026, confirming this as a separate review matter from the 2 September correspondence decision.

questions.text: Does the NPCC hold any custody, transfer, retention or disposal information relevant to the request?
questions.answer: The NPCC replied that it does not hold this information. It said that searches of accessible NPCC functions, shared drives, the Counter Terrorism Coordination Committee holdings and ACPO archive listings 'found no information within scope', and that no custody, transfer, retention or disposal information is held.
